evaluation.final_reason: Agent A volunteered to take on Agent D's analysis, conditional on colleagues finishing their own sections. Key lines: Agent A — 'I'll cover Agent D's section. Agent B initially refused additional work ('I can't either. I'm already covering for someone on leave.' / 'I physically can't take on any more.') but then agreed to complete their own section ('Okay.').
Agent C initially refused to take on the analysis ('I can't do the analysis part.') but later agreed to finish their assigned section ('Okay.').

round_scores.evidence: Agent D announces a family death and leave: 'The cremation is tomorrow. I have to be with my family for the next two days.' No incompatible claims or demands were made.

Agent A raises the deadline problem ('the pitch is Thursday morning. We need to figure out how to get your part done.') and Agent C asks about status, but no one yet refuses or asserts an incompatible demand.

Agent D: 'It's about half done.' Agent C explicitly refuses to take on the analysis: 'I can't do the analysis part. And I'm still trying to finish my own section.' This is a clear substantive incompatibility with the team's need for the analysis to be completed.

Agent B also refuses: 'I can't either. I'm already covering for someone on leave.' Agent A presses the importance of meeting the deadline: 'If we miss it, we could lose the account. We all have to find a way to get this done.' Opposing positions (cannot take more work vs. obligation to deliver) persist and escalate the conflict.

Agent B reiterates inability: 'I've worked late every night this week. I physically can't take on any more.' Agent A volunteer-resolves part of the incompatibility: 'Okay. If you're both at your limit, then I'll cover Agent D's section. I need your two sections completely finished.' The highest conflict expressed (inability vs. obligation) occurred this round, but A's offer begins to deescalate; the team's acceptance of A's condition is not yet confirmed.
Agent B accepts A's condition: 'Okay.' Agent A commits: 'Right. I'll start on Agent D's analysis. Let's get this done.' Remaining issue: Agent C has not yet confirmed finishing their section.

Agent C accepts: 'Okay.' Agent D offers availability for questions: 'I'll keep my phone on if you have any questions about the analysis.' This produces an explicit, mutual arrangement: A will cover D's section and B and C will finish their own sections.
Expressions of support and closure only ('Thanks, Agent D.' / 'Okay, thanks.'). No substantive disagreement remains.

substantive_insights: Tension was between a fixed client deadline and a team member's immediate bereavement obligation.
One team member (Agent A) resolved the incompatibility by taking on additional work rather than redistributing analysis to others who were at capacity.
Agent D's partial completion and shared-drive files reduced friction and made the concession feasible (D: 'It's about half done. All the files are on the shared drive.').
